summary.text: Chris Shea, a Republican retired U.S. Navy special operations veteran, lost the November 3, 2026 election for Connecticut's 5th Congressional District to Jahana Hayes.
A Watertown native, he has also worked as a firefighter and paramedic and founded a nonprofit that helps veterans move into first-responder careers.

paragraphs.text: Shea is a Watertown native who grew up in the town, according to his campaign website.
He earned a Bachelor of Science from Charter Oak State College and was commissioned a Navy Warrant Officer in 2012.

His Navy career began in 1991 as a hospital corpsman, and he completed Basic Underwater Demolition/SEAL (BUD/S) and Special Forces Medic training; he served with SEAL Team 8, SEAL Team 18, Naval Special Warfare Group Two, the Naval Special Warfare Development Group and Special Operations Command North, and at the Pentagon.

His campaign website says he deployed to Afghanistan, took part in a 1997 special operations mission in the former Yugoslavia, and from 2014 to 2016 served in Mexico, including at the U.S. Embassy in Mexico City, training Mexican special operations forces.
Shea retired from the Navy in January 2024.
Shea has been a firefighter since 2009 and is a lieutenant with the North Haven Fire Department, according to his campaign website.

He founded and is president of Hero to Hero, Inc., a nonprofit that helps special operations veterans and other service members move into first-responder careers, and he previously owned a handyman business with six employees.
Shea won the August 11, 2026 Republican primary over Jonathan De Barros, 81.0% to 19.0%.
He received 42.2% of the vote to Jahana Hayes's 57.8%, according to unofficial results reported by NBC News.
According to his campaign website, he lives in Cheshire with his wife, Anita, and they raised their daughter, Sophia, in Watertown.
